glossary.Band-like: Feeling like a tight band around the head.
glossary.Pressing: A steady pressure or squeezing pain rather than throbbing.
glossary.Stress: Mental or emotional strain, a common headache trigger.
glossary.Muscle tension: Sustained tightening of muscles, here in the scalp, neck and shoulders.
glossary.Neurological exam: Examination of nerves, power, reflexes, sensation, coordination and cranial nerves.
glossary.Tenderness: Pain when an area is pressed.
glossary.Neurological signs: Abnormal findings on neurological examination, such as weakness or visual loss.
glossary.Gold standard: The most accurate, definitive way to make a diagnosis.
glossary.Clinical diagnosis: A diagnosis made from history and examination without needing tests.
glossary.Secondary cause: An underlying disease, such as a bleed or tumour, causing the headache.
glossary.Causative medication: The drug responsible for causing the symptom.
glossary.Abruptly: Stopped all at once, without tapering.
glossary.Withdraw gradually: Reduce the dose step by step to avoid withdrawal symptoms.
glossary.Opioid analgesia: Painkillers acting on opioid receptors, such as codeine and morphine.
glossary.Peripheral: Outside the brain and spinal cord.
glossary.Central: Within the brain and spinal cord.
glossary.Pain pathways: The nerve routes carrying pain signals to the brain.
glossary.Poor posture: Holding the body in a strained position, which tightens neck and scalp muscles.
glossary.Dehydration: Too little water in the body.
glossary.Trigeminal nerve: Cranial nerve V, carrying sensation from the face and meninges.
glossary.Downregulates: Turns down the activity or number of a system or receptor.
glossary.Pain modulation: The brain's own system for turning pain signals up or down.
glossary.Paradoxically: In the opposite way to what you would expect.
glossary.Triggers: Factors that set off an attack, such as poor sleep or stress.
